sentences.text: Its feet possessed fused bones, a structure similar to those found in modern birds.
The animal lacked a furcula, or wishbone, meaning it could not have held the muscles required for flight.
It also had very short femurs, a feature typical of animals adapted for running.
José Bonaparte named the species Patagopteryx deferrariisi in 1992 after receiving fossils from Oscar de Ferrariis.
The skeleton shows clear signs that its ancestors were capable of flying.
Known through multiple specimens, it constitutes the best-represented Mesozoic bird in the Southern Hemisphere.
Today, although still considered a bird, Patagopteryx is isolated in a separate family or order within the Ornithuromorpha.
This creature lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 80 million years ago, in the Sierra Barrosa of northwestern Patagonia, Argentina.
Its specific time range falls within the Santonian stage, from 85.7 to 83.6 million years ago.
It is debated whether Patagopteryx represents the earliest example of secondary flightlessness, as other studies suggest earlier diverging theropods may also have been secondarily flightless.
